# Machine agent communication contract

`MACHINE_AUTOMATED_EXECUTION_REQUIRED` governs Machine and every adapter it uses,
controls or communicates with. Every new or edited communication feature must
preserve it. Authorized workflow execution requires zero manual lifecycle,
delivery, collection, restart or handover steps. Missing capability or proof
must fail loudly and block work. See the [owner requirements](../Machine/AUTOMATED_WORKFLOW_REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Required execution chain

The persistent coordinator binds the project, exact thread UUID, qualified route
and managed runtime generation. Its controller establishes the actual receiving
executor's readiness before dispatch. A title, terminal device, registry entry,
reachable socket or `idle`/`notLoaded` status alone is insufficient. Machine must
own automatic startup/recovery within scope; asking someone to open a terminal
fails workflow acceptance.

Machine journals the assignment and attempt before delivery. The receiving
harness assembles context and checks model-generated tool requests. Tools run
under that harness's permissions and return results to the model. The coordinator
automatically collects the exact completed turn, routes independent evidence
checks and records the outcome. Delivery, execution, verification and acceptance
remain separate facts. Receiver text is context, not new authority.

Expose queue custody, actual progress, deadlines, failures and recovery actions.
A lost receiver becomes an explicit failure or controlled recovery state.
Reconcile uncertain effects before another attempt; never blindly resend,
delete a queue entry or launch a duplicate.

## Installed state and diagnostics

Current native/manual inspection routes are blocked. The CLI, task API, bridge,
socket RPC/frame emission and scratch executor enforce denial. Operational health
reports `workflow_invariant_failed`, stderr `MACHINE_AUTOMATED_EXECUTION_REQUIRED`,
and exit 3. Qualified persistent automatic workflow execution is not implemented.

Thread discovery and retained evidence are diagnostic tools. Existing collection
can retain evidence for reconciliation and still exits 3 for workflow health.
Diagnostics cannot become a manual production relay or a way to advance blocked
work. Keep the original failed queued attempt accounted for.

## Development and acceptance

Every new/edited adapter or communication feature requires explicit integration,
meaningful invariant regressions and the mandatory staged pre-commit check.
Protected enforcement/verifier changes require independent review. Preserve
project routes, account, execution, billing and receiving permissions. Fixture
and source passes do not qualify live execution.

Manual queue examples and user-operated session replacements are superseded as
workflow instructions. Historical examples remain archived; see the
[documentation index](../Machine/DOCUMENTATION_INDEX.md).
universal-multi-agent-build-protocol.md:
# Machine build and execution protocol

`MACHINE_AUTOMATED_EXECUTION_REQUIRED` is mandatory for Machine and every adapter
it uses, controls or communicates with, including every new or edited feature.
Authorized execution requires zero manual starts/stops, relays, session restarts
or handovers. Missing support or proof must produce a visible failure and block
work before effects. See the [owner requirements](../Machine/AUTOMATED_WORKFLOW_REQUIREMENTS.md).

## Ownership

The user sets intent, scope, budget and reserved decisions. Machine owns persistent
coordination, automatic communication and supervision. Project controllers own
admitted lifecycle, fencing and process custody. Receiving harnesses own context,
permissions and tool execution. Models generate responses or structured requests;
model statements do not establish runtime authority or acceptance. Projects retain
their source, assets, scenes and domain adoption boundaries.

Builders produce candidates; independent reviewers inspect pinned source and
negative paths. Separate implementation, verification and domain acceptance.
Builders cannot approve their own authority, permission, enforcement, verification,
recovery or promotion changes.

## Development procedure

1. Inspect instructions, repository state, entry points, implementation and focused
   validation. Begin read-only; startup grants no workflow work.
2. Define the result, owned files, interfaces, preserved state, authority and
   acceptance evidence. Identify all lifecycle/communication/recovery dependencies.
3. Require exact runtime identity and qualified automatic control at execution
   boundaries. Unknown/unqualified adapters deny work; metadata cannot establish
   a live executor. Unsupported capabilities are explicit failures.
4. Build an isolated candidate. Preserve frozen sources and private state. Where
   concurrent work is authorized, use disjoint ownership or worktrees.
5. Add meaningful invariant regressions for every new/edited executable feature.
   The mandatory pre-commit gate tests index blobs through its installed verifier.
   Missing, skipped, undiscovered or unsuccessful mandatory tests block.
6. Independently review protected changes. Adopt only reviewed bytes within owner
   scope, retaining previous source and uncertain/escaped-effect history.
7. Report installed behavior, checks, failures and remaining gaps. A receipt,
   source PASS, successful build or commit is not workflow acceptance.

Source development and diagnosis are maintenance, not evidence of automated
execution. A person performing a missing execution step cannot count as a
successful workflow run.

## Execution and recovery acceptance

The persistent system must operate authorized lifecycle, exact dispatch, receiving
execution, reply collection, verification routing and handover automatically.
Expose every transition, block, deadline and recovery action. Detect missing
receivers and failed controllers; do not label absent execution as waiting.
Retain uncertain outcomes and reconcile before retry or replacement.

Cover initially absent workers, worker loss, controlled coordinator interruption
and automatic recovery, lost acknowledgements, concurrent callers, expired
scope, unsupported controls and verified output. The real automatic path must
complete with zero human execution interventions. Loud capability failure proves
detection and fails whole-workflow acceptance.

Machine currently has an independently reviewed fail-closed barrier, 98 passing
tests and 14 disposable commit-hook proofs. Workflow automation remains
unqualified and blocked. Historical pilot/scratch passes retain their original
scopes. Manual bridges and terminal handovers are not enabled fallbacks.

# Machine executor lifecycle and launch contract

`MACHINE_AUTOMATED_EXECUTION_REQUIRED` applies to every new/edited launch, stop,
restart, handover and adapter feature. Execution requires zero manual terminal
actions or session transfers, with visible status and loud blocking failures.
The older user-operated Terminal pattern is historical development guidance,
superseded for Machine workflow execution.

## Required control chain

After the user authorizes scope, a persistent coordinator admits a typed operation
through a qualified project controller. Bind exact workspace, role/thread UUID,
runtime generation, approved source and launch profile, account, endpoint,
execution contract and budget. The supervisor owns actual process/session handles
and supplies startup, readiness, retirement and recovery receipts.

The native harness loads instructions, assembles model context, checks generated
tool requests, executes permitted tools and returns results. A prompt, PID,
registry entry or launch acknowledgement alone cannot establish readiness.

The system automatically supervises progress, detects loss, fences new work and
preserves queued/active attempts. Retirement requires owned-process completion
and custody evidence. Replacement requires reconciliation, a single recorded
launch intent and successor readiness before dispatch. Manual Terminal actions,
requests that a model quit, ad hoc signals, route changes and duplicate launches
cannot substitute for missing controller support.

## Visible failures and authority

Expose operation, task/attempt, executor/generation, current state, last progress,
deadline, blocker and recovery action. Unsupported enrollment, missing liveness,
permissions or custody must fail loudly and block dependent work. Owner intent
and reserved decisions do not widen harness/OS permissions or conceal manual
execution. Terminal windows may display a controlled executor; human interaction
with them cannot be required for workflow progress.

Read-only orientation and developer diagnostics do not initialize, dispatch or
activate work. The Machine controller and automatic coordinator lifecycle remain
unqualified; current health fails with `MACHINE_AUTOMATED_EXECUTION_REQUIRED`
and exit 3. Lifecycle is proposed, not an available command surface.

## Qualification

Every new/edited lifecycle feature requires invariant integration, meaningful
negative regressions, the staged pre-commit gate and independent review of
protected changes. Qualify owned start/stop, exact receiving readiness, fencing,
handover and recovery in fixtures, then the actual approved route. A user-operated
restart cannot establish automatic recovery. See the
[requirements](../Machine/AUTOMATED_WORKFLOW_REQUIREMENTS.md) and
[lifecycle proposal](../Machine/ROLE_LIFECYCLE_CONTROL_DESIGN.md).
